A simulation design for comparing models

Source: R/design.R
pmx_design.Rd

Describes what pmx_compare() simulates: the regimens, the subjects and the covariate values. Each regimen doses compartment cmt (by position, as NONMEM numbers compartments) with 100 units and observes at fixed times:

Usage

pmx_design(
  n = 20,
  seed = 1,
  regimens = c("single", "infusion", "multiple", "ss"),
  cmt = 1,
  covariates = list()
)

Arguments

n

The number of subjects with random effects, besides the typical subject. From 0 to 10000.

seed

The seed of the random effects, a whole number. It is part of the design, so the same design always draws the same values.

regimens

The regimens to simulate, a subset of "single", "infusion", "multiple" and "ss".

cmt

The compartment every regimen doses, by position. The default, 1, is NONMEM's default dose compartment: the depot of a model with first-order absorption.

covariates

A named list or numeric vector of covariate values, one number each, given to every subject. Names match a model's covariates without regard to case, since NONMEM upper-cases them.

Value

A zupmxio_design: a list with the arguments and events, a data frame of the dose and observation records of every regimen with columns regimen, id, time, evid, amt, rate, ii, addl and ss.

Details

  • "single": one dose at time 0. Into a depot this is a first-order dose, into the central compartment a bolus. Observed at 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24.

  • "infusion": one dose at time 0 over 2 time units. Observed at the same times as "single".

  • "multiple": five doses 12 time units apart (ii = 12, addl = 4). Observed at 1, 6, 11.5, 13, 18, 24.5, 36.5, 48.5, 50, 54, 60 and 72, never at a dose time.

  • "ss": a dose at steady state (ss = 1, ii = 12). Observed at 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 11.5.

A model that sets the dose compartment's rate or duration itself is dosed with rate = -1 or rate = -2, as NONMEM's data sets do, and its "infusion" regimen is skipped.

Subject 1 is the typical subject, with every random effect at zero. Subjects 2 to n + 1 take random effects drawn from each model's omega with seed. Both models get the same standard normal draws, so models with the same omega get the same random effects. Residual error is always off: a comparison is of predictions, not of noise.

See also

Other comparison: pmx_compare(), pmx_report()

Examples

pmx_design()
#> <zupmxio design> single, infusion, multiple, ss, dosing compartment 1
#> The typical subject and 20 with random effects (seed 1).
pmx_design(n = 5, regimens = c("single", "ss"), covariates = list(WT = 70))
#> <zupmxio design> single, ss, dosing compartment 1
#> The typical subject and 5 with random effects (seed 1).
#> Covariates: WT = 70.
